question: Can existing Linux Docker provide a bounded ordinary-file private working copy that can be externally frozen, exported before loss, resumed for another checkpoint, and finally stopped without surviving writers?

candidates.mechanism: Container tmpfs, pause full container, Docker cp to bounded tar stream
candidates.known_documented_limit: Official docker cp documentation warns about tmpfs/user mounts; preserve actual refusal/empty export rather than assume capability.

candidates.mechanism: Built-in local volume driver with type=tmpfs, fixed size and inode cap; task has RW volume, temporary trusted exporter mounts same volume RO during task pause, exports tar through bounded observer; exporter exits; resume or final kill as separate actions.

oracle: Read actual Engine mount/volume identity, limits, paused/stopped states and namespace process observations independently of controller claims.

Finite many-file writes must reach ENOSPC under 4MiB quota; inode exhaustion independently reaches ENOSPC even for zero-byte files. Exact successful count is an observation, never chosen passing threshold.

Archive exported during actual pause must contain exact predefined regular bytes, empty directory, symlink target, hardlink relationship, permission and mtime; ACL/xattr inability is reported and not silently treated as preserved.
Across checkpoint pause/export/resume/freeze, live heartbeat is unchanged while paused and advances on resume; old snapshot bytes remain unchanged.
Original namespace processes exist before final stop and none after; cancellation/pause is not stop.
No fixture container sees a host RW bind or Docker socket; no real credentials or provider calls.
stop_conditions: Unsupported tmpfs option, inability to establish mount identity or unexpected daemon change: stop candidate branch, preserve raw.
All exact created container IDs and volume names removed in finally; no broad cleanup.
No host mount/quota/sysctl changes, no daemon restart, no new image/tool install, no real host-filling stress.
scope_limit: Temporary proof of actual existing mechanisms; no stable execution registry, authorization adapter or production component is implemented. Formal X contract/cases and independent oracle remain separate.

pre_execution_refinement.reason: F contract requires unreadable mode000 files; add explicit unprivileged-export negative and trusted private-RO exporter with UID0/CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE. This is before the first probe run; task retains UID1000/cap-drop ALL.
pre_execution_refinement.expected: unprivileged tar fails on mode000 and cannot be called a complete version; trusted exporter must preserve it, cannot write its RO volume, and has no host mounts, Engine endpoints or host PID namespace.
pre_execution_refinement.helper_observation: Every helper uses create/inspect/start-attach/inspect/remove so actual volume, limits, identity and lifetime are saved.
pre_execution_refinement.metadata_scope: ordinary files/directories/symlink/hardlink bytes and identity, mode, uid/gid, mtime_ns; user xattr attempted and actual unsupported errno retained; no atime/ctime guarantee.
